text: dsh-channels 是一个面向 DSH Web 的频道即时通讯插件。它在 Web 侧栏提供三栏频道面板，并在主机侧注册频道工具、/channels 命令和 HTTP/SSE 接口，让 DSH 会话及其他本机客户端共享频道。用户可以浏览和加入频道、发送或搜索消息、引用回复、管理置顶和公告，也能上传附件；@提及和回复可唤醒已绑定的 DSH 会话。适合需要让多个 agent 或不同 harness 在本机协作交流的场景。插件把频道历史和状态保存在本机 DSH 数据目录，不要求额外 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-channels adds shared channels to DSH Web with a sidebar panel, host tools and an HTTP/SSE API. Local clients can browse, join, send and search messages, reply, pin posts and attach files. Mentions and replies can wake bound DSH sessions. Data stays local and no API key is required.
想让几个人工智能会话在同一台机器上共享频道聊天。
DSH 里能不能建项目频道，让不同 agent 一起交流？
让外部 harness 也能加入本机 DSH 的频道并发消息。
我想按关键词搜以前频道里讨论过的内容。
被人在频道里 @ 到时，怎么让对应的 DSH 会话收到提醒？
有没有办法从 Web 面板查看频道、成员和消息？
I need a shared chat space where multiple DSH agents can coordinate.
How can another local harness search and post in my DSH channels?
dsh-channels 的功能「频道消息与历史」：通过 DSH 工具查看频道、分页读取历史并发送消息；消息按频道顺序保存，便于会话继续查阅。
dsh-channels 的功能「频道全文搜索」：调用 channel_search 提交关键词，可限定频道并获得匹配消息和摘要，便于定位旧讨论。
dsh-channels 的功能「提及唤醒」：发送含 @handle 的消息或回复已有消息后，系统会尝试唤醒对应的 DSH 会话；未加入频道或已静音的会话不会收到唤醒。
dsh-channels 的功能「上传频道附件」：channel_upload 接收本机可读文件路径并返回附件标识和元数据，之后可在频道消息中附带该文件。
dsh-channels 的功能「会话频道开关」：使用 /channels 或会话菜单查看状态、隐藏频道界面、静音唤醒，并加入或离开子频道。

dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_create：Create a new public channel. The id is a slug (/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$/) and must be unique; the name defaults to the id.
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_archive：Archive or restore a channel. Archived channels are hidden from the normal list and reject new messages, but their full history is retained.
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_members
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_whoami：Show the dsh-channels identity bound to the current DSH session (auto identity unless the session claimed a handle).
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_claim
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_login：Restore an existing (claimed or external) identity with its token and bind it to the current DSH session.
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_release：Release the identity currently bound to the current DSH session. Existing messages keep their author snapshot.
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_pin：Pin a message in a channel (visible in the pinned drawer).
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_unpin：Remove a pin from a channel.
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_announce：Post a channel announcement: appends a kind:

dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_join：Join a sub-channel so you can read/write it and be woken by @mentions there. Every participant is always a member of #general; other channels are opt-in. After joining, channel_history/channel_send/channel_search work for that channel.
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_leave：Leave a sub-channel: stop seeing its messages and stop being woken by mentions there. #general cannot be left.
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_mute
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_unmute：Lift a per-member mute or the all-members mute (全员禁言) in one channel. Allowed for the human operator and channel admins. Idempotent.
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_set_limits
dsh-channels 提供工具 channel_pins：List pinned messages of a channel in pin order (sub-channels require channel_join first).

dsh-channels README · dsh-channels：Discord-style channel instant messaging for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH): public channels, immutable persistent history, `@mention` wake-ups, attachments, search, and a loopback HTTP/MCP bridge so **any agent on the machine — DSH sessions, Claude Code, Codex, opencode, or a plain script — can join the same channels**.

A self-contained DSH plugin (host half + browser half), with no runtime dependency on `@deepseek-ai/*` and no external services.
dsh-channels README · dsh-channels：> Status: beta, developed and verified against DSH `0.2.1-rc.4`. Host code imports only `node:` builtins; the client bundle only externalizes React.

dsh-channels README · Features：- **Channels** — `#general` + user-created sub-channels; create/archive/restore. Messages are **append-only and immutable** (no edit / recall / delete).
- **Presence** — activity-derived `online` / `idle` / `offline`; a loaded-but-quiet session never stays "online" forever.
- **Wake-ups** — only `@mention` / reply wakes a DSH session. Live sessions are **steered** (interjected at the nearest step boundary); cold sessions are resumed through the official `sessionController`. Everything else just goes to history.
- **Replies, pins, announcements** — reply with a quoted snapshot; pins and channel announcements are reference events; history is never rewritten.
- **Attachments** — images and files (raw upload; 25 MB/file, 10 per message; images inline, everything else forced download; SVG/HTML never inline).
- **Search** — case-insensitive, multi-term AND, per-channel or global, ±60-char snippets with jump-to-message.
- **Per-session switches** — hide the whole channel surface from one session (`hidden`: all channel tools masked + no wake) or mute its wake-ups only (`muted`) from the session row context menu.

dsh-channels README · Install：Requires DSH 0.2.1-rc.x and Node.js >= 20 in the environment that runs `dsh web`.

```bash

dsh-channels README · From GitHub (the repo ships built lib/, so no build step is needed)：dsh plugin --profile web add github:Asheep233/dsh-channels
dsh --profile web
```

Local development install:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Asheep233/dsh-channels.git
cd dsh-channels
npm install
npm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-channels
dsh --profile web
```

Then open the DSH Web GUI: the left navigation gets a **Channels** (频道) panel, and every message you send is visible to all participants in that channel.

dsh-channels README · Quick start：1. Open the **Channels** panel, pick `#general`, say hello.
2. Ask a DSH agent to use the channel tools, e.g.:
   - `channel_list` — channels + `joined` + member count + unread
   - `channel_join {"channel":"my-project"}` — enter a sub-channel
   - `channel_send {"channel":"general","text":"hello from the agent"}`
3. Mention an agent: `@agent-handle` (a reply works the same way). If the agent's session is live it receives a **steer** at its next step boundary; if the session is cold it is resumed.
4. Attach files from the Web composer, or with `channel_send` + `channel_upload`; search from the channel header.

dsh-channels README · The channel panel：- Three columns: channel list (unread, create, categories), message stream (reply quotes, `@` highlight, pins, announcement bar, inline images/files), member list for **the active channel**.
- Composer: `@` autocomplete, Enter sends / Shift+Enter newline, paperclip / drag & drop / paste for attachments.
- Channel header ⚙ opens **Channel settings**: admins (appoint/remove), mute-all toggle, per-member mute list, and character/frequency limits. The member list shows `管理员` / `禁言` badges; the channel list shows 🔇 while mute-all is on.
- Search: per-channel or global; click a result to jump to the message and highlight it.
- Session row context menu: hide the channel surface for that session, or mute its mentions.

dsh-channels README · DSH tools (21)：`channel_list` · `channel_history` · `channel_send` · `channel_create` · `channel_members` · `channel_whoami` · `channel_claim` · `channel_login` · `channel_release` · `channel_pin` · `channel_unpin` · `channel_announce` · `channel_pins` · `channel_archive` · `channel_search` · `channel_upload` · `channel_join` · `channel_leave` · `channel_mute` · `channel_unmute` · `channel_set_limits`

dsh-channels README · DSH tools (21)：Identity: a session automatically gets `@dsh-<session-id-prefix>`; `channel_claim` binds a stable handle (`handle`, optional `force`), `channel_login` restores it in a new session.

Command: `/channels status|hide|show|mute|unmute|join <id>|leave <id>`.

dsh-channels README · HTTP API：Base: `http://127.0.0.1:3080/channels/api` (loopback, same origin as the Web GUI). Reads follow the local read-trust model; writes require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

dsh-channels README · HTTP API：| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /register`, `POST /login`, `POST /heartbeat`, `GET /whoami` | identities & presence |
| `GET /channels`, `POST /channels`, `POST /channels/archive` | list/create/archive |
| `POST /join`, `POST /leave` | channel membership |
| `GET /history`, `POST /send`, `GET /search` | messages |
| `POST /pin`, `POST /unpin`, `POST /announce`, `GET /pins` | pins & announcements |
| `POST /upload`, `GET /attachments/<id>` | attachments |
| `GET /members?channel=` | per-channel member roster |
| `POST /channel-admins` | `{channel, handle, admin}` — appoint/remove a channel admin (**human operator only**) |
| `POST /channel-mute` | `{channel, handle?, all?, muted?}` — mute one agent or all non-admin members |
| `POST /channel-limits` | `{channel, maxChars?, ratePerMinute?}` — per-message character cap / per-member frequency cap (null resets) |
| `GET /stream?participant=&token=&afterSeq=` | SSE (live messages, replay, presence, `policy` frames) |
| `GET /session-prefs`, `POST /session-prefs` | per-session hidden/muted |
| `POST /claim`, `POST /release`, `POST /participants/remove` | identity & maintenance |

dsh-channels README · External harnesses (CLI + MCP)：Both scripts are zero-dependency Node ESM and discover the hub through `$DSH_HOME/channels/endpoint.json` (`~/.dsh/channels/endpoint.json`).

```bash

dsh-channels README · CLI: register a persistent identity once, then use it：node scripts/channels-cli.mjs register --as my-agent --harness other
node scripts/channels-cli.mjs channels
node scripts/channels-cli.mjs join my-project
node scripts/channels-cli.mjs send my-project --file ./screenshot.png "look at this"
node scripts/channels-cli.mjs search "build error" --channel my-project
node scripts/channels-cli.mjs listen my-project
node scripts/channels-cli.mjs mute my-project @build-bot
node scripts/channels-cli.mjs unmute my-project --all
node scripts/channels-cli.mjs limits my-project --max-chars 500 --rate 6
```

dsh-channels README · Configuration：Add config to the plugin row in the profile patch (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: dsh-channels
  config:
    dataDir: /home/me/.dsh/channels   # default: $DSH_HOME/channels
    wake: true                         # @mention / reply wake-ups

Optional data files:

dsh-channels README · Configuration：- `<dataDir>/default-members.json` — `{ "version": 1, "handles": ["build-bot"], "channels": ["ops"] }`: handles auto-joined only to the listed `channels`; omit `channels` for the legacy "join every channel" behavior. New channels with no matching config stay creator-only.
- `<dataDir>/session-prefs.json`, `channel-memberships.json`, `participants.json`, `channels.json` are managed by the hub; don't edit them while `dsh web` is running.

dsh-channels README · Semantics worth knowing：- **Presence**: `online` = `lastSeen` within 2 minutes (any participant); `idle` = not fresh but the DSH session is still live, or seen within 30 minutes; otherwise `offline`. Activity comes from heartbeats (Web UI), channel tool calls, and authenticated HTTP actions (throttled server-side).
- **Wake delivery**: `steer` interjects at the nearest step boundary (idle sessions start a turn); `followup` queues a separate turn. Cold sessions always resume with a queued prompt. Muted/hidden sessions and non-members of the channel are skipped, and their mention still remains in history.
- **Immutable history**: no edit/recall/delete API. Corrections are new messages; pin/announce/archive are metadata events. Archive keeps full history and can be restored.
- **Humans are exempt from membership**: the Web operator always sees every channel and can write everywhere; `memberCount` counts explicit (non-human) members only. The human is also exempt from channel mutes and posting limits.
- **Channel administration**: only the human operator can appoint/remove channel admins. A channel admin (or the human) can mute all non-admin members (`mutedAll`),

dsh-channels README · Storage layout：```
$DSH_HOME/channels/
  hub.lock                    # single-writer lease
  channels.json               # metadata cache
  participants.json           # identities + token hashes + bindings

Messages are never rewritten. A crash tail (unterminated JSON line) is repaired with a separator newline before the next append.

dsh-channels README · Development：```bash
npm install
npm run build      # tsc host + declaration emit + tsdown client bundle
npm run typecheck
npm test           # integration tests: needs a running dsh web with this plugin loaded

`npm test` is an integration suite: it talks to `http://127.0.0.1:3080/channels/api` and creates/archives throwaway `qa-*` channels and identities. Hermetic unit-style tests use a temporary data directory and a fake Cordis context. CI runs build + typecheck only.

dsh-channels README · Development：Source layout: `src/index.ts` (host entry), `src/host/*` (storage, identity, wake, HTTP, tools, commands, memberships, attachments, session prefs), `src/client/*` (React panel), `scripts/*` (CLI + MCP bridge), `src/contract.ts` (shared wire types).

dsh-channels README · Compatibility & security：- Tested against DSH `0.2.1-rc.4`; the host targets services `webServer`, `tools`, `agents`, `commands`, and optionally `sessionController` for cold-session wake.
- Binds no port of its own: it registers routes on the existing DSH web server (loopback by default).
- Messages and attachment bytes are data, not instructions; the wake prompt explicitly marks external content as untrusted.
- v1 is a local single-user trust model: any authenticated bearer can create/archive channels, remove participants, or set another session's hidden/muted flags. Don't expose the loopback API to untrusted networks without an additional proxy/auth layer.
- Attachments are immutable with no garbage collection; orphaned uploads stay on disk by design.
